title: Choose the visual world for Too Many Books
question: The roll assigned Fahrplan. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Fahrplan
options.lineage: Swiss railway departure posters and printed timetables
options.thesis: Your library as a timetable: every Work a row, every Reading a departure, every gap left honestly blank.
options.viewport: iPad landscape: a ruled Library table on ink black, yellow column heads, a red badge on Inbox, and the selected Work's page as a side panel.
options.risk: Could read cold or utilitarian if type and spacing are not warm; needs real covers to carry the charm.

raised.raise: Every row edits in place where it sits, so browsing and correcting are one gesture.
Stats counts sit in fixed decimal columns, so a year's total reads like a physical counter.

options.case: Dense, scannable, and honest about unknowns (blank cells, not guesses). Long Inbox sessions get a departures-board rhythm that makes a backlog feel finishable.

options.label: Banded Paperback
options.thesis: Each Work is a small jacket: strict bands, one saturated colour per Genre, covers doing the talking.
options.viewport: A wall of covers on a strict three-band grid, Genre colour on each spine edge, quiet white chrome around them.
options.risk: Familiar to anyone who knows Penguin; lowest-risk of the bookish worlds and the one most runs land on.

options.label: Box Stack Archive
options.lineage: sneaker archive walls, cardboard boxes with end labels
options.thesis: The library is a wall of boxes: end label on show, pull one out to open the Work.
options.viewport: A stacked wall of end-labels: title in condensed caps, author and format as mono size-run.
options.case: Literally 'too many books' as a stack, and Work pages open like lids; loses narrowly on clarity for dense filtering.
options.risk: Charm can slow a 500-Work library on a filter-heavy task.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps and control descriptions
options.thesis: Reading history as terrain with your route drawn in purple across it.
options.viewport: White forest ground, contour lines, purple numbered controls; Inbox items are controls you punch off.
options.case: Punching controls is a lovely Inbox ritual and Stats fit terrain; loses on Library clarity because books are not places.
options.risk: Metaphor stretches thin on Add and Settings.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: airline ticket wallets, carbon coupons, VOID stamps
options.thesis: Loans are coupons; dismissed ones are stamped VOID, never deleted.
options.viewport: Tabbed coupon heads, hairline fare boxes, carbon-purple numerals, a red VOID stamp on dismissed rows.
options.case: Maps almost one-to-one to Inbox and Import records; loses narrowly on identification because it is about travel.
options.risk: Library and Stats have to stretch the coupon idea.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.case: Loses both: retro novelty, and cover art has nowhere to live in one-bit.
options.kept: In-place editing of anything on screen.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.case: Loses both: glowing dark chrome around a book app, and only Stats benefits.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean cover-grid library app with a tab bar and rounded cards, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, a grid of covers, star ratings and shelves in native iPad idiom.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other trackers by design.
